records.title: Comparative Analysis and Adaptation Strategies of Vision Foundation Models in Dermoscopic Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate segmentation of skin lesions is of critical clinical importance for early melanoma diagnosis; however, the direct application of large foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to medical images characterized by low contrast and fuzzy boundaries remains insufficient due to substantial domain gaps. In current study, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy is presented by integrating lightweight adapter modules into a frozen Vision Transformer backbone. The proposed SAM-Adapter approach was comparatively evaluated against the original SAM and MedSAM models on the publicly available ISIC2018 and HAM10000 dermoscopic datasets. Optimized with AdamW, the model achieved the highest Dice (0.9603) and IoU (0.9241) scores along with the lowest HD95 (22.57) value on the HAM10000 dataset. Validated as statistically significant via the Wilcoxon test, this approach minimized computational overhead while demonstrating superior accuracy in boundary delineation. This adapter-based framework is planned for integration into clinical decision-support systems and other medical imaging modalities.

records.title: Automated segmentation and quantification of histological liver features for MASH/MASLD scoring
records.abstract: Abstract The increasing global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) creates an urgent need for objective histopathological assessment. Conventional histological approaches are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, we propose a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline for the segmentation and characterisation of histological liver features of MASH/MASLD. Segmentation was applied to H&E sections from 45 mice and 44 humans with MASH/MASLD. Our qHisto (quantitative histology) method, is nnU-Net-based and quantifies key histological components of the MASH-score, including steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation and ballooning. Additionally, we determined novel features that are inaccessible through manual histology, like the distribution of fat droplet sizes, nuclear aspect ratio and heatmaps. qHisto parameters showed strong positive correlations with conventional histology scores (fat: R = 0.91, inflammation: R = 0.70, ballooning: R = 0.47) and with hepatic fat fraction by magnetic resonance imaging ( R = 0.87). Our novel scores showed that nuclei deformation is driven by large fat droplets rather than the overall amount of fat. A key advantage of our method is spatially resolved, precise histological quantification to provide detailed assessment of disease severity. By automating time-consuming and repetitive readouts, qHisto improves standardisation and reproducibility of MASH/MASLD feature quantification and provides scalable, slide-wide analysis that supports histopathologists and enhances clinical assessment.

records.title: Ideal Point Fusion for Reliable Morphometry of Lunar Regolith Particles
records.abstract: Lunar regolith particle morphology is critical for particle classification and representative sample selection. Morphometric measurements also provide key parameters for discrete element modeling and the development of regolith simulants with controlled particle shapes. However, their accuracy depends directly on segmentation quality. This study investigates whether combining measurements from complementary segmentation models can improve accuracy across morphological descriptors. The fusion leaves the source masks unchanged. The objective is to develop and evaluate Morphology-Aware Ideal-Point Fusion (MIPF). MIPF evaluates each model in three dimensions: region completeness, boundary accuracy, and false-positive suppression. Ideal-point analysis assigns higher scores to models closer to the best observed performance and farther from the worst. MIPF uses descriptor-specific weights for these scores to determine each model’s contribution. Area-based indices place more weight on region completeness, while contour-based indices emphasize boundary accuracy. MIPF then retains the two highest-weighted models and combines their measurements without generating a new mask. In a ground-truth comparison based on dataset-level means for 15 morphological indices, MIPF ranks first for six indices and second for the remaining nine, giving an average rank of 1.60. Its median relative error is 11.56%, compared with 12.96% for U-Mamba, 13.73% for nnU-Net, 15.30% for OffSeg, and 31.18% for SegFormer. Although MIPF does not minimize the error for every index, it achieves the most consistent overall performance and reduces the dependence of aggregate morphometric results on any single segmentation model.

records.title: Automated Sinus MRI Phenotyping with PARASIDE: Construct-Specific Validation Against Independent Manual Annotations and Radiological Assessments in a Population-Based Cohort
records.abstract: Manual sinus magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) annotations are valuable but difficult to scale. We evaluated PARASIDE, an nnU-Net-based framework for automated sinus compartment segmentation on T1-weighted MRI, against historical manual annotations and radiological assessments generated independently of PARASIDE within the same longitudinal Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP) imaging population. We linked 12,867 sinus sides from 3217 participants. Primary construct–marker pairings were specified before endpoint-specific modelling. Soft-tissue fraction discriminated abnormal sides in frontal (AUC 0.850, 95% CI 0.832–0.868) and maxillary sinuses (AUC 0.828, 95% CI 0.816–0.841). The topographic marker showed moderate discrimination of basal from apical opacification (AUC 0.746 left; 0.782 right), while total frontal volume discriminated aplasia/hypoplasia ratings (AUC 0.988); the near-absence threshold remained highly specific but insensitive. Primary findings were robust to exclusion of 279 participants overlapping with the original PARASIDE development population. Historical maxillary volumetric masks showed strong agreement, whereas frontal agreement improved after accounting for the predefined inferior extent of the non-equivalent historical segmentation approach. Polyposis remained weakly separable. PARASIDE showed correspondence with distinct, anatomically measurable MRI phenotypes across complementary historical reference layers, while morphology-specific constructs required dedicated reference standards.

records.title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Periodontal Diseases Using Cone‐Beam Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review
records.abstract: AIM: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have shown promise for the detection of periodontal disease. This study aimed to synthesize current evidence on the diagnostic performance of AI models applied to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) for periodontal disease. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted to identify studies on AI-assisted diagnosis of periodontal disease using CBCT published up to December 2025. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool was used to assess the risk of bias. RESULTS: Among 10,099 records screened, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies indicate that AI models, predominantly based on convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures applied to CBCT images, have substantial potential for detecting periodontal bone loss and related conditions. However, diagnostic performance metrics varied markedly across studies, and direct comparisons with human clinicians produced inconsistent findings, underscoring the need for more rigorous study designs and standardized datasets. CONCLUSIONS: Despite limitations arising from heterogeneous methodologies and non-standardized data collection, CBCT-based AI models show considerable promise for enhancing periodontal disease diagnosis. Further high-quality, methodologically robust research is warranted to validate and optimize these approaches for clinical use. TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD420251273846.

records.title: Promise and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation: a feasibility study
records.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the feasibility and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation and deep learning-based segmentation.ApproachWe developed ChameleonNet, a framework utilizing the Contrastive Unpaired Translation (CUT) network with decoupled contrastive learning (DCL) loss to synthesize noncontrast CT from contrast CT scans. Using annotations of four heart chambers (left atrium (LA), left ventricle (LV), right atrium (RA), and right ventricle (RV)) from contrast scans, we trained a Hausdorff distance loss-enhanced nnU-Net on synthesized noncontrast images. The translation model was trained with 35,538 contrast-enhanced and 37,197 noncontrast CT slices. The segmentation model was trained with 292 synthesized noncontrast scans. Performance was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 95th Hausdorff distance (HD95) on 36 synthesized noncontrast scans, and volume agreement on 36 real noncontrast CT scans was assessed using Pearson correlation, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and mean percentage error (MPE).ResultsThe segmentation model achieved DSC of 0.94 (±0.01), 0.91 (±0.04), 0.92 (±0.03), 0.93 (±0.02), and HD95 of 3.63 (±1.49), 5.74 (±4.08), 5.18 (±1.77), and 5.51 (±3.21) mm on synthesized noncontrast images for LA, LV, RA, and RV, respectively. On real noncontrast CT scans, Pearson correlations were 0.93, 0.82, 0.87, and 0.89 (all p<0.001), with MAPE ranging from 9.22% to 20.79%, and MPE ranging from −12.52% to 4.67%.ConclusionsChameleonNet demonstrated feasibility for heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT without manual noncontrast annotations. However, volume errors, particularly for LV and RV, indicate that further refinement and validation are needed before clinical use.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma microvascular invasion based on magnetic resonance imaging feature extraction artificial neural network
records.abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence is highly correlated with increased mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is indicative of aggressive tumor biology in HCC. AIM To construct an artificial neural network (ANN) capable of accurately predicting MVI presence in HCC using magnetic resonance imaging. METHODS This study included 255 patients with HCC with tumors < 3 cm. Radiologists annotated the tumors on the T1-weighted plain MR images. Subsequently, a three-layer ANN was constructed using image features as inputs to predict MVI status in patients with HCC. Postoperative pathological examination is considered the gold standard for determining MVI. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm. RESULTS Using the bagging strategy to vote for 50 classifier classification results, a prediction model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79. Moreover, correlation analysis revealed that alpha-fetoprotein values and tumor volume were not significantly correlated with the occurrence of MVI, whereas tumor sphericity was significantly correlated with MVI (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION Analysis of variable correlations regarding MVI in tumors with diameters < 3 cm should prioritize tumor sphericity. The ANN model demonstrated strong predictive MVI for patients with HCC (AUC = 0.79).

records.title: Deep Neural Network and Radiomics-based Magnetic Resonance Imaging System for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
records.abstract: Background: Accurate preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is crucial for surgeons to make informed decisions regarding appropriate treatment strategies.However, it continues to pose a significant challenge for radiologists.The integration of computer-aided diagnosis utilizing deep learning technology emerges as a promising approach to enhance the prediction accuracy.Methods: This experiment incorporated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans with six different sequences.After a cross-sequence registration preprocess, a deep neural network was employed for the segmentation of hepatocellular carcinoma.The final prediction model was constructed by combining radiomics features with clinical features.The selection of clinical features for the final model was determined through univariate analysis.Results: In this study, we analyzed MRI scans obtained from a cohort of 420 patients diagnosed with HCC.Among them, 140 cases exhibited MVI, while the remaining 280 cases comprised the non-MVI group.The radiomics features demonstrated strong predictive capability for MVI.By extracting radiomic features from each MRI sequence and subsequently integrating them, we achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.794±0.033.Specifically, for tumor sizes ranging from 3 to 5 cm, the AUC reached 0.860±0.065.Conclusions: In this study, we present a fully automatic system for predicting MVI in HCC based on preoperative MRI.Our approach leverages the fusion of radiomics and clinical features to achieve accurate MVI prediction.The system demonstrates robust performance in predicting MVI, particularly in the 3-5 cm tumor group.

records.title: Radiogenomics nomogram based on MRI and microRNAs to predict microvascular invasion of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to develop and validate a radiogenomics nomogram for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) on the basis of MRI and microRNAs (miRNAs). Materials and methods: This cohort study included 168 patients (training cohort: n = 116; validation cohort: n = 52) with pathologically confirmed HCC, who underwent preoperative MRI and plasma miRNA examination. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were used to identify independent risk factors associated with MVI. These risk factors were used to produce a nomogram. The performance of the nomogram was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis was performed to determine whether the nomogram was clinically useful. Results: The independent risk factors for MVI were maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21 (all P < 0.001). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score of the nomogram in the validation cohort were 0.970, 0.722, 0.884, and 0.916, respectively. The AUC of the nomogram was 0.900 (95% CI: 0.808-0.992) in the validation cohort, higher than that of any other single factor model (maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21). Conclusion: The radiogenomics nomogram shows satisfactory predictive performance in predicting MVI in HCC and provides a feasible and practical reference for tumor treatment decisions.

records.title: Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma and Its Prognostic Implications: A Multicenter Study
records.abstract: Introduction: Previous studies on preoperative predictors of microvascular invasion (MVI) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICCA) have presented inconsistent results. This study aimed to identify preoperative clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) factors that can predict MVI in ICCA and to evaluate their prognostic utility using a multicenter cohort. Methods: A multicenter cohort of 446 patients who underwent preoperative MRI and surgical resection for ICCA at six tertiary referral institutions between 2009 and 2018 was analyzed for clinical, pathologic, and MR imaging characteristics. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify significant predictors of pathologically confirmed MVI, which were subsequently used to stratify patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups based on the number of predictors identified. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank test were conducted to assess long-term survival and early recurrence among the three groups. Results: Among the 446 patients (mean age, 63.0 ± 9.9 years; 277 men), 234 (52.5%) had MVI on pathology. Independent predictors of MVI included serum carbohydrate antigen 19–9 levels (≥80 U/mL; odds ratio [OR]: 2.68, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.64–4.37, p < 0.001), tumor size (≥4 cm; OR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.01–2.54, p = 0.046), tumor multiplicity (OR: 2.84, 95% CI: 1.58–5.12, p < 0.001), and arterial phase peritumoral enhancement (OR: 2.83, 95% CI: 1.81–4.42, p < 0.001). Stratifying patients by MVI risk – low (no predictors), intermediate (1–3 predictors), and high (4 predictors) – revealed a significant decrease in both recurrence-free and overall survival rates (p < 0.001), along with a corresponding increase in early recurrence rates (p < 0.001) as the risk level increased. Conclusion: Risk stratification utilizing four key predictors can effectively assess the risk of MVI in ICCA and is associated with postoperative outcomes.

records.title: Interpretable and generalizable deep learning model for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion and outcome in hepatocellular carcinoma based on MRI: a multicenter study
records.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop an interpretable, domain-generalizable deep learning model for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective dataset of 546 HCC patients from five centers, we developed and validated a clinical-radiological model and deep learning models aimed at MVI prediction. The models were developed on a dataset of 263 cases consisting of data from three centers, internally validated on a set of 66 patients, and externally tested on two independent sets. An adversarial network-based deep learning (AD-DL) model was developed to learn domain-invariant features from multiple centers within the training set. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated using pathological MVI status. With the best-performed model, early recurrence-free survival (ERFS) stratification was validated on the external test set by the log-rank test, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with MVI status were tested on the RNA sequencing analysis of the Cancer Imaging Archive. RESULTS: The AD-DL model demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance and generalizability with an AUC of 0.793 in the internal test set, 0.801 in external test set 1, and 0.773 in external test set 2. The model's prediction of MVI status also demonstrated a significant correlation with ERFS (p = 0.048). DEGs associated with MVI status were primarily enriched in the metabolic processes and the Wnt signaling pathway, and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition process. CONCLUSIONS: The AD-DL model allows preoperative MVI prediction and ERFS stratification in HCC patients, which has a good generalizability and biological interpretability. CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: The adversarial network-based deep learning model predicts MVI status well in HCC patients and demonstrates good generalizability. By integrating bioinformatics analysis of the model's predictions, it achieves biological interpretability, facilitating its clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Current MVI assessment models for HCC lack interpretability and generalizability. The adversarial network-based model's performance surpassed clinical radiology and squeeze-and-excitation network-based models. Biological function analysis was employed to enhance the interpretability and clinical translatability of the adversarial network-based model.

records.title: Preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma with a radiological feature-based nomogram: a bi-centre study
records.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a nomogram for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the radiological features of enhanced CT and to verify two imaging techniques (CT and MRI) in an external centre. METHOD: A total of 346 patients were retrospectively included (training, n = 185, CT images; external testing 1, n = 90, CT images; external testing 2, n = 71, MRI images), including 229 MVI-negative patients and 117 MVI-positive patients. The radiological features and clinical information of enhanced CT images were analysed, and the independent variables associated with MVI in HCC were determined by logistic regression analysis. Then, a nomogram prediction model was constructed. External validation was performed on CT (n = 90) and MRI (n = 71) images from another centre. RESULTS: Among the 23 radiological and clinical features, size, arterial peritumoral enhancement (APE), tumour margin and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) were independent influencing factors for MVI in HCC. The nomogram integrating these risk factors had a good predictive effect, with AUC, specificity and sensitivity values of 0.834 (95% CI: 0.774-0.895), 75.0% and 83.5%, respectively. The AUC values of external verification based on CT and MRI image data were 0.794 (95% CI: 0.700-0.888) and 0.883 (95% CI: 0.807-0.959), respectively. No statistical difference in AUC values among training set and testing sets was found. CONCLUSION: The proposed nomogram prediction model for MVI in HCC has high accuracy, can be used with different imaging techniques, and has good clinical applicability.

records.title: Accuracy of artificial intelligence models integrating machine learning and deep learning in detecting microvascular invasion in liver cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.abstract: e16184 Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a global health challenge, ranking sixth in incidence and third in cancer-related mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a crucial prognostic marker influencing recurrence rates and survival. Accurate preoperative MVI detection can guide surgical planning but is limited by invasive histopathological exams and interobserver variability. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), in predicting MVI in HCC using imaging modalities such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, PET/CT, and histopathology. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines, covering studies from 2010 to 2023. Comprehensive searches were conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, European PMC, and BioMed Central. AI models were assessed for diagnostic accuracy using QUADAS-2 and Radiomics Quality Score (RQS). Metrics like the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were analyzed. Results: This meta-analysis synthesized data from 51 studies, encompassing 6,257 records. DL models showed a pooled AUC of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.80–0.86), with sensitivity and specificity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75–0.82) and 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79–0.88), respectively. ML models achieved a pooled AUC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.80–0.86), sensitivity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.71–0.85), and higher specificity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84–0.92). Across imaging modalities, MRI and CT-based models achieved pooled AUCs of 0.87 and 0.83 for DL and 0.85 and 0.82 for ML, respectively. Ultrasound-based models demonstrated higher specificity but slightly lower sensitivity. Models incorporating clinical features did not outperform purely radiomics-based approaches. Quality assessments revealed low bias risks in patient selection (88%), index tests (94%), and reference standards (98%). However, only 51% of studies addressed inter-scanner variability, and 55% incorporated calibration or resampling. The mean RQS was 40%, with 84% adhering to robust imaging protocols. Conclusions: AI models, particularly DL, exhibit robust accuracy in predicting MVI in HCC, showing promise for integration into clinical workflows. These tools could enable personalized preoperative planning, improving patient outcomes and reducing recurrence risks. Standardized protocols, prospective validation, and broader adoption of advanced AI methods are needed to ensure consistent clinical utility and cost-effectiveness.

records.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
records.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

records.title: LIVER CANCER DETECTION USING RESNET, SWIN TRANSFORMER AND CONVNEXT TINY NETWORKS
records.journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
records.abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. Another challenge is that slices from the same patient can be very similar, which may cause data leakage when splitting the data randomly. This study focuses on classifying liver CT slices into Tumor and No-Tumor classes using deep learning. The LiTS and 3Dircadb datasets are combined and used for the experiments. Three deep learning models, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50, are trained and evaluated. A patient-level data split is used to keep patients in the training, validation, and test sets separate. The three models are also combined using a soft-voting ensemble. The final evaluation is performed on an unseen test set containing 6,323 slices. The soft-voting ensemble achieved the highest accuracy of 92.74%. These results show that the models can detect tumor and no-tumor slices, while the class imbalance remains an important challenge for tumor detection.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI
records.abstract: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. This study encoded feature variations across multi-phase MRI sequences for the preoperative prediction of MVI. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). All of them underwent preoperative MR examination and were randomly partitioned into training and testing cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. Radiomics features were subsequently extracted from both the original and expanded ROIs. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Among all evaluated combinations, the Fourier-inspired temporal encoding method combined with an ExtraTrees classifier, applied to the original tumoral ROI with a 5-mm peritumoral expansion, achieved the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.850 (95% CI: 0.675–0.978). Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

records.title: A multiparametric liver MRI dataset with multiple tumor and liver segmentations of pre-treatment hepatocellular carcinomas
records.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays a key role for HCC screening, diagnosis and treatment planning, the development of AI models for detection and characterization of focal liver lesions is hindered by the scarcity of publicly available annotated MRI datasets. Here, we present OpenSwissHCC, a curated multiphasic dataset of 132 multiparametric DCE-MRI scans from adult patients with chronic liver disease acquired on 1.5 T and 3 T MRI scanners between 2011 and 2020. The dataset includes both HCC-positive (n = 63) and HCC-negative (n = 69) patients, with up to five lesions per patient segmented across each sequence when confidently identified. Whole-liver and lesion segmentations were manually performed and expert-validated, with lesion metadata including LI-RADS scores, size, liver segment location, major LI-RADS imaging features (non-rim APHE, washout, capsule, threshold growth) and key ancillary/background findings (e.g., mosaic architecture, fat/blood products, necrosis, tumor-in-vein; cirrhosis and portal-hypertension signs). In total, 140 lesions were annotated, including 97 confirmed HCC. Additionally, we provide liver masks for all T1-weighted images (T1-WI) sequences, generated using a pre-trained nnU-Net model, as well as pre-computed transforms to facilitate registration across T1-WI phases. By providing a comprehensive, well-annotated, and standardized collection of liver MRI examinations, OpenSwissHCC aims to assist the development and benchmarking of advanced computational methods for automated HCC detection, segmentation, and characterization, fostering progress toward precision imaging and personalized treatment planning.

records.title: Head-to-head comparison of [18F]FAPI and [18F]FDG PET/CT in the clinical value of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: To investigate the clinical utility of fluorine-18-labeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor ([ 18 F]FAPI) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) relative to [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([ 18 F]FDG) PET/CT for tumor detection and staging in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. A cohort of 38 individuals (median age, 61 years; interquartile range, 56–68 years), all with pathologically confirmed primary or recurrent HCC, were enrolled. All participants underwent both [ 18 F]FDG and [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT. Maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), FAP expression tumor volume (FTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), total lesion FAP expression (TLF), and clinical staging were compared. Each patient had at least one intrahepatic lesion confirmed by surgical resection or percutaneous biopsy. Histopathologic confirmation was available for 46/66 intrahepatic lesions, 3/56 lymph-node (LN) metastases, and 4/33 distant metastases; the remaining lesions were adjudicated using a composite reference standard based on multimodal imaging follow-up and treatment response. Additionally, correlations between PET imaging findings and serum biomarkers, comprising alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II), were analyzed. The cohort included 32 primary and 6 recurrent HCC cases. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection rates than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic lesions (96.7% vs. 60.0%; p < 0.001), LN metastases (94.6% vs. 80.4%; p = 0.021), and distant metastases (78.8% vs. 48.5%; p = 0.002). For primary intrahepatic lesions, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.90 vs. 4.80, p < 0.001) and TBR (5.45 vs. 2.60, p < 0.001) than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT. In the patient-level volumetric analysis of the 32 initial-staging patients, FTV was 21.04 vs. MTV 13.75 ( p < 0.001), and TLF was 135.36 vs. TLG 51.44 ( p < 0.001). For LN metastases, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.98 vs. 6.63, p = 0.048) and TBR (7.85 vs. 4.95, p < 0.001), as well as higher FTV than MTV (6.55 vs. 4.55, p < 0.001) and TLF than TLG (67.65 vs. 52.75, p < 0.001). Positive correlations were observed between [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT tumor uptake parameters and AFP and PIVKA-II levels (nominal p < 0.05). Relative to [ 18 F]FDG, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT produced staging changes in 19/32 patients undergoing initial staging, including 6 true upstagings, and identified 3 additional local recurrences; a FAPI-informed management change was implemented in 57.9% (22/38) of patients. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.947, 0.921, 0.895, and 0.864 for SUVmax, TBR, FTV, and TLF, respectively. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection in selected HCC settings than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic, lymph-node, and distant metastatic lesions and may provide complementary information for staging and treatment planning in this preliminary single-center cohort. records.title: Foundation Model‐Enabled Pathology‐Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
records.abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

records.title: Combined analysis of preoperative circulating tumor cells status and tumor size to guide width of resection margin for solitary hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Background The optimal resection margin width for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains controversial. The purpose of this study was to explore the value of preoperative circulating tumor cells (CTCs) status and tumor size in guiding the resection margin width of patients with HCC. Methods This study was a multicenter retrospective study that included 383 patients who underwent resection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Preoperative circulating tumor cell (CTC) detection (CTC ≥ 1/CTC = 0) and imaging evaluation of tumor size (≤ 3 cm/> 3 cm) were performed in all patients. We aimed to compare recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) between patients receiving narrow (< 1 cm) and wide (≥ 1 cm) resection margins. Results Tumor diameter and CTC status were independent predictors of RFS and OS in the entire cohort. In patients with tumor diameter ≤ 3 cm, CTC-positive status correlated with poorer RFS but not OS. RFS and OS of narrow margin group and wide margin group were similar, and there was no statistical significance (P > 0.05). In the patients with tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-negative group, the RFS and OS of the narrow margin group were comparable to those of the wide margin group (P > 0.05). However, in patients with tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-positive groups, RFS and OS were better in the wide margin group than in the narrow margin group (P < 0.05). Conclusions Using preoperative CTC status and tumor diameter as preoperative markers, combined analysis of CTC status and tumor diameter could help to determine surgical margin width in patients with solitary HCC. Narrow margins are indicated for patients with a tumor diameter ≤ 3 cm (regardless of CTC status) and for patients with a tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-negative. Whereas wide margins are preferred in patients with tumors > 3 cm in diameter and CTC-positive.

records.title: CT habitat and peritumoral radiomics for predicting progression after repeat TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study
records.abstract: Background This study developed and validated an machine-learning-based radiomics model integrating tumor habitat radiomics, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features to predict progression-free survival (PFS) following repeat transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to training (n = 94) and internal validation (n = 41) cohorts, while Centers 2 (n = 82) and 3 (n = 53) served as external validation cohorts. Tumor habitats and 5-mm peritumoral regions were generated from contrast-enhanced CT images. Radiomics features were selected using univariate Cox and LASSO-Cox regression. A fusion model and HPC risk score were constructed by integrating selected radiomics signatures and clinical variables. Performance was assessed using time-dependent ROC, C-index, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan–Meier analyses. Results The optimal habitat cluster number was K = 2. Eleven habitat features, three peritumoral features, and alpha-fetoprotein were retained in the fusion model. The model achieved AUCs of 0.923, 0.921, and 0.897 for 3-, 6-, and 9-month progression-free survival in the training cohort, and 0.932, 0.863, and 0.916 in the internal validation cohort, respectively; all external AUCs exceeded 0.82. The fusion model showed higher C-index values than the clinical model across cohorts. High-risk patients had significantly shorter PFS than low-risk patients (all P < 0.001). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility. Conclusion The CT-based fusion model and HPC risk score effectively predicted progression risk in HCC.

records.title: Intratumoral habitat combined with peritumoral radiomics to improve the predictive performance of initial TACE efficacy: a multicenter retrospective study
records.abstract: Background and purpose Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the primary treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, significant heterogeneity in patient response to TACE necessitates non-invasive and precise methods for evaluating treatment efficacy. This study aims to explore the predictive ability of combined intratumoral habitat imaging and peritumoral radiomics features for TACE response. Materials and methods We retrospectively enrolled HCC patients who underwent TACE treatment at four centers between January 2015 and December 2023. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced MRI. Patients from centers A and B formed the training cohort, while those from centers C and D comprised external validation cohorts. Using three-phase enhanced MRI (arterial, portal venous, and delayed phase), K-Means clustering divided intratumoral regions into three habitat subregions (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), and peritumoral features were extracted. Clinical variables were also collected. Key radiomics features were selected by LASSO regression, and clinical indicators were identified through univariable and multivariable logistic regression. The XGBoost algorithm constructed intratumoral, peritumoral, clinical, and combined models. Performance was evaluated using ROC curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and DeLong tests. Results A total of 174 HCC patients who underwent initial TACE treatment were enrolled, including 104 in training and 70 in validation cohorts. Fifteen key intratumoral features from the habitat subregions and 24 radiomics features from the peritumoral region were identified, primarily derived from wavelet transforms and texture analysis. The wavelet-LLL_glszm_ZoneVariance_ PVP feature from Cluster 2 contributed significantly to the model and had a positive impact (highest SHAP value). Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (P = 0.015) and Tumor size (P = 0.016) remained significantly associated with TACE treatment response in multivariable analysis. The combined model based on clinical, intratumoral habitat and peritumoral radiomics showed superior predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.950 (95% CI: 0.89-1.00), 0.850 (0.79-0.91) and 0.830 (0.77-0.89) in training and validation cohorts, outperforming single models (Clinic: AUC = 0.700, Tumor_Habitat: AUC = 0.880, Peritumor_Radiomics: AUC = 0.870, P<0.05). Calibration and DCA demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes and favorable net benefit across the evaluated threshold probabilities. Conclusion The combined model integrating AFP, Tumor size, intratumoral habitat imaging, and peritumoral radiomics could accurately predict initial TACE response in HCC patients. Cluster 2-derived features showed relatively greater contributions among the intratumoral habitat subregions. This non-invasive prediction tool may provide complementary information for pretreatment risk stratification. Future prospective multicenter studies are needed to verify the clinical applicability of the model.

records.title: A Review of Street Scene Semantic Segmentation: Current Status, Challenges, and Future Prospects
records.abstract: Street scene semantic segmentation is a core task in environmental perception for autonomous driving, which has made significant progress in recent years driven by deep learning. This paper systematically reviews the current research status in this field, analyzes technical challenges, and explores future development directions. First, it examines the technological evolution of traditional machine learning and deep learning methods, focusing on model innovations based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformer architectures. Then, it discusses cutting-edge solutions such as multimodal fusion, self-supervised learning, and 3D segmentation to address key challenges, including complex scene understanding, real-time constraints, and data efficiency. Finally, in the context of smart transportation and urban digital management, it proposes pathways to overcome technical bottlenecks, providing theoretical references for future research and practical applications.

records.title: Current progress of digital twin construction using medical imaging
records.journal: Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics
records.abstract: Medical imaging is fundamental to digital twin technology, enabling patient-specific virtual models of anatomy and physiology. By integrating high-resolution modalities (Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Computed Tomography (CT), Positron Emission Tomography (PET), ultrasound) with computational frameworks, recent imaging advances now support real-time simulation, predictive modeling, and earlier disease detection. Such capabilities directly inform individualized treatment planning and contribute to more precise, personalized care. Despite remaining challenges-complex anatomical modeling, multimodal integration, and high computational demands-recent advances in imaging and machine learning have significantly enhanced the accuracy and clinical utility of digital twins. The main contributions of our review are: (1) a system-by-system classification of methodologies; (2) evidence that advanced imaging modalities have improved diagnostic accuracy, treatment effectiveness, and patient outcomes beyond conventional approaches; and (3) identification of remaining technical bottlenecks. We further analyze key technical barriers-such as data scarcity and computational complexity-and outline future directions (e.g., AI-driven data augmentation, real-time model optimization) to unlock digital twins' full potential in precision medicine.

records.title: Three-dimensional Imaging and Scanning: Current and Future Applications for Pathology
records.abstract: Imaging is vital for the assessment of physiologic and phenotypic details. In the past, biomedical imaging was heavily reliant on analog, low-throughput methods, which would produce two-dimensional images. However, newer, digital, and high-throughput three-dimensional (3D) imaging methods, which rely on computer vision and computer graphics, are transforming the way biomedical professionals practice. 3D imaging has been useful in diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic decision-making for the medical and biomedical professions. Herein, we summarize current imaging methods that enable optimal 3D histopathologic reconstruction: Scanning, 3D scanning, and whole slide imaging. Briefly mentioned are emerging platforms, which combine robotics, sectioning, and imaging in their pursuit to digitize and automate the entire microscopy workflow. Finally, both current and emerging 3D imaging methods are discussed in relation to current and future applications within the context of pathology.

records.title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical performance of deep learning models for grading diabetic retinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.abstract: Background: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable visual impairment worldwide, and its precise severity grading is critical for optimizing clinical management. Conventional frameworks, notably the International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) scale, are often hindered by substantial inter-observer variability and high dependency on specialist expertise. While deep learning (DL) has recently emerged as a transformative approach for automated stratification, a comprehensive synthesis of evidence regarding its diagnostic performance and clinical application remains lacking. Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively assess the diagnostic accuracy of fundus image-based deep learning models in the grading of diabetic retinopathy. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for relevant studies published up to October 28, 2025. Diagnostic accuracy studies utilizing DL algorithms alongside ICDR criteria for diabetic retinopathy grading were included. Literature screening and data extraction were performed independently by two researchers, and the risk of bias was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool. Results: A total of 41 studies were included, encompassing various DL architectures and multiple public and private fundus image datasets. In the five-class classification task based on ICDR criteria, the pooled sensitivities of DL-based models varied significantly across severity levels: 95.19% (95% CI: 93.00%-97.00%) for no DR (stage 0), 72.06% (95% CI: 62.06%-81.09%) for mild NPDR (stage 1), 84.33% (95% CI: 78.90%-89.10%) for moderate NPDR (stage 2), 75.84% (95% CI: 68.42%-82.57%) for severe NPDR (stage 3), and 78.82% (95% CI: 71.76%-85.13%) for PDR (stage 4). In the simplified four-class classification task, sensitivities markedly improved across all grades: 96.85% (95% CI: 90.18%-99.93%) for stage 0, 92.94% (95% CI: 79.50%-99.72%) for stage 1, 92.75% (95% CI: 79.31%-99.61%) for stage 2, and 88.19% (95% CI: 68.99%-98.93%) for stage 3. Conclusion: DL exhibits high sensitivity and substantial potential for DR grading, particularly in screening for no DR and vision-threatening DR. Nevertheless, precisely differentiating between adjacent non-proliferative stages remains a clinical challenge. The observed heterogeneity underscores the imperative for methodological standardization, rigorous external validation, and multimodal data integration. Future research should prioritize enhancing clinical utility and generalizability to facilitate their translation into real-world clinical practice. Systematic Review Registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261338867.

records.title: Advances in proton therapy technology and global clinical applications
records.abstract: Proton therapy, by leveraging its unique physical characteristic of the Bragg peak, enables high-precision dose delivery to the tumor target while effectively protecting surrounding normal tissues, and has become an important representative of advanced radiotherapy. This review aims to systematically summarize key technological breakthroughs in recent years that have driven the progress of proton therapy, including compact superconducting accelerators, pencil beam scanning (PBS), image-guided proton therapy (IGPT), and the transformative ultra-high dose rate FLASH radiotherapy, while highlighting the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing proton therapy toward real-time adaptive precision radiotherapy. The article also explores the global distribution and development status of proton centers, with a specific analysis of China's notable advancements as an emerging market in center construction, equipment localization, and the treatment of characteristic local tumor types. Moving forward, it is essential to continue promoting technological integration and innovation, strengthen high-quality clinical research, and develop a more accessible, intelligent, and personalized proton therapy system to achieve broader clinical application and patient benefit.

records.title: A novel CycleGAN network applicable for enhancing low-quality ultrasound images of multiple organs
records.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
records.abstract: Medical ultrasound imaging is one of the most commonly used imaging modalities for clinicians to make clinical diagnoses. Currently, medical ultrasound imaging equipment is transitioning towards portable ultrasound devices that can be more widely used. However, portable ultrasound devices suffer from the drawback of low imaging quality due to hardware limitations. Enhancing ultrasound images requires paired medical ultrasound image data with identical content but different styles for enhancement training, which is quite challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a DPM CycleGAN, a generative adversarial network that can convert low-quality ultrasound images into high-quality ones without the need for paired data. This network employs a maximum perception feature extraction module designed specifically for ultrasound images to extract global features. Subsequently, a diffusion feature enhancement module integrated with pseudo-labels is used to enhance these global features. The generator of DPM CycleGAN utilizes the enhanced global features to generate high-quality medical ultrasound images. Experimental results on the USenhance 2023 ultrasound dataset demonstrate that this method can effectively enhance low-quality ultrasound images of various organs, not only improving the resolution of ultrasound images but also enhancing the organ structure and texture information, and eliminating some noise in the ultrasound images. Compared with the latest ultrasound image enhancement methods, the model proposed in this paper performs optimally in all metrics, which fully demonstrates the promising potential of the proposed method in medical image enhancement and its valuable support in areas such as disease prediction and treatment.

records.title: Unveiling the role of spatial transcriptomics in the analysis of the tumor immune microenvironment (Review)
records.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment plays a decisive role in tumor initiation, progression and therapeutic response. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables comprehensive analysis of the whole transcriptome or specific gene sets while preserving the original spatial location information within tissues, offering a revolutionary approach to unraveling the complexity of the tumor immune microenvironment in the spatial dimension. The present review aims to systematically elaborate on the role and application of ST in deciphering the tumor immune microenvironment. Focusing on tumor microenvironment niches at different stages of tumor progression, from precancerous lesions and locally advanced tumors to distant metastasis, recent advances in ST for mapping the spatial distribution and functional states of key cell subpopulations are summarized. The present review further highlights its potential for clinical translation in identifying spatially defined biomarkers and elucidating the mechanisms underlying therapeutic responses and analyze the key technical challenges that constrain the application of ST in clinical practice. In recent years, the rapid development of machine learning algorithms has provided new opportunities to overcome the technical limitations of ST. The deep integration of machine learning with ST is laying a solid theoretical foundation and technical support for precision medicine and early intervention.

records.title: Automatic segmentation and classification of the liver tumor using deep learning algorithms
records.journal: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)
records.abstract: Liver tumors are one of the life-threatening cancers with the fastest-growth rates worldwide. Early detection of tumors may therefore reduce morbidity and increase the survival rate. The development of automated techniques for the precise segmentation of hepatic tumors is essential for assisting doctors in tumor diagnosis and preoperative planning for surgical treatment of the liver which reduces the risk of surgical resection. The classification and segmentation of hepatic tumors in Computerized Tomography (CT) scan pose a great challenge due to noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, and variability in tumor tissue appearance, shape, size, and location. In this study, we describe a novel method for automatic segmentation and classification of hepatic tumors in CT scan images using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks. For tumor segmentation, we created a modified Dense U-net model. The classification framework is based on a novel deep CNN with a pre-trained VGG-16 network to distinguish between normal and malignant liver tumors. The proposed system was evaluated based on MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge dataset and obtained the best result with a Dice Score of 95.40%, Jaccard Index of 92%, and accuracy of 92.60% for segmentation and the classification model has achieved an accuracy of 96%, Sensitivity of 95.80%, Specificity of 96.20% and Precision of 95.80%.

records.title: Comparison of two‐dimensional and three‐dimensional iterative watershed segmentation methods in hepatic tumor volumetrics
records.abstract: In this work the authors compare the accuracy of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) implementations of a computer-aided image segmentation method to that of physician observers (using manual outlining) for volume measurements of liver tumors visualized with diagnostic contrast-enhanced and PET/CT-based non-contrast-enhanced (PET-CT) CT scans. The method assessed is a hybridization of the watershed method using observer-set markers with a gradient vector flow approach. This method is known as the iterative watershed segmentation (IWS) method. Initial assessments are performed using software phantoms that model a range of tumor shapes, noise levels, and noise qualities. IWS is then applied to CT image sets of patients with identified hepatic tumors and compared to the physicians' manual outlines on the same tumors. The repeatability of the physicians' measurements is also assessed. IWS utilizes multiple levels of segmentation performed with the use of "fuzzy regions" that could be considered part of a selected tumor. In phantom studies, the outermost volume outline for level 1 (called level 1_1 consisting of inner region plus fuzzy region) was generally the most accurate. For in vivo studies, the level 1_1 and the second outermost outline for level 2 (called level 2_2 consisting of inner region plus two fuzzy regions) typically had the smallest percent error values when compared to physician observer volume estimates. Our data indicate that allowing the operator to choose the "best result" level iteration outline from all generated outlines would likely give the more accurate volume for a given tumor rather than automatically choosing a particular level iteration outline. The preliminary in vivo results indicate that 2D-IWS is likely to be more accurate than 3D-IWS in relation to the observer volume estimates.

records.title: Semi-automatic detection of hepatic tumor in computed tomography images
records.abstract: Abstract In this work, the main purpose is develop a computational segmentation strategy for liver tumor semiautomatic detection. This strategy considers three-dimensional computed tomography images and it consists of techniques application that, on the one hand, diminish the noise and detect the edges of the objects present in those images and, on the other hand, generate the liver tumor morphology. For this, the sequence of techniques composed of gaussian smoothing, gradient magnitude, median filter, region growing and binary morphological dilation are used. The value obtained, for the metric called Dice score, show a good correlation between manual segmentation, performed by a hepatologist, and the tumor segmentation obtained using the proposed technique. This type of segmentation is the extreme utility for the characterization of hepatic tumors and the planning of the clinical behavior to be followed in the treatment of this human liver disease.

records.title: Radiofrequency ablation of liver tumors: quantitative assessment of tumor coverage through CT image processing
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is one of the most promising non-surgical treatments for hepatic tumors. The assessment of the therapeutic efficacy of RFA is usually obtained by visual comparison of pre- and post-treatment CT images, but no numerical quantification is performed. METHODS: In this work, a novel method aiming at providing a more objective tool for the evaluation of RFA coverage is described. Image registration and segmentation techniques were applied to enable the visualization of the tumor and the corresponding post-RFA necrosis in the same framework. In addition, a set of numerical indexes describing tumor/necrosis overlap and their mutual position were computed. RESULTS: After validation of segmentation step, the method was applied on a dataset composed by 10 tumors, suspected not to be completed treated. Numerical indexes showed that only two tumors were totally treated and the percentage of a residual tumor was in the range of 5.12%-35.92%. CONCLUSIONS: This work represents a first attempt to obtain a quantitative tool aimed to assess the accuracy of RFA treatment. The possibility to visualize the tumor and the correspondent post-RFA necrosis in the same framework and the definition of some synthetic numerical indexes could help clinicians in ameliorating RFA treatment.

records.title: LiverNet: Diagnosis of Liver Tumors in Human CT Images
records.abstract: Liver cancer contributes to the increasing mortality rate in the world. Therefore, early detection may lead to a decrease in morbidity and increase the chance of survival rate. This research offers a computer-aided diagnosis system, which uses computed tomography scans to categorize hepatic tumors as benign or malignant. The 3D segmented liver from the LiTS17 dataset is passed through a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to detect and classify the existing tumors as benign or malignant. In this work, we propose a novel light CNN with eight layers and just one conventional layer to classify the segmented liver. This proposed model is utilized in two different tracks; the first track uses deep learning classification and achieves a 95.6% accuracy. Meanwhile, the second track uses the automatically extracted features together with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier and achieves 100% accuracy. The proposed network is light, fast, reliable, and accurate. It can be exploited by an oncological specialist, which will make the diagnosis a simple task. Furthermore, the proposed network achieves high accuracy without the curation of images, which will reduce time and cost.

records.title: Automatic Segmentation of hepatic tumors in CT Images using Adaptive EM and Diagnostics of IR Spectroscopy
records.journal: Asia International Conference on Quantitative InfraRed Thermography (QIRT Asia)
records.abstract: Arial, 9pt, bold)The paper introduces the automated segmentation of hepatic tumor from abdominal Computed Tomography images and diagnose it using IR spectroscopy.In this context, a segmentation algorithm for liver tumor is developed, which helps to diagnose the tumor by segmenting the affected tumor area.A hybrid diagnosis method, Adaptive EM is proposed to detect the hepatic lesions automatically by utilizing sequential images of abdominal CT.An area function adaptation scheme that uses EM model grows the clusters without the need for initial selection of clusters.Infrared (IR) spectroscopic imaging of human liver tissue slices has been used to identify and characterize liver tumors, by giving a discriminative model of nucleus and cytoplast of tumor, incorporating texture, layout, and context information efficiently.Both training and testing dataset are preprocessed to produce texton map.The feature responses of each image in the training data set is calculated and are trained efficiently in AdaBoost classifier using Conditional Random Field and Piecewise Training methods.The proposed method provides high classification and segmentation accuracy for nucleus of tumor that are exceedingly textured in IR spectroscopic image.This work also suggests utility for these methods beyond the identification of liver tumors.

records.title: Effect of Blood Vessel Segmentation on the Outcome of Electroporation-Based Treatments of Liver Tumors
records.abstract: Electroporation-based treatments rely on increasing the permeability of the cell membrane by high voltage electric pulses applied to tissue via electrodes. To ensure that the whole tumor is covered with sufficiently high electric field, accurate numerical models are built based on individual patient anatomy. Extraction of patient's anatomy through segmentation of medical images inevitably produces some errors. In order to ensure the robustness of treatment planning, it is necessary to evaluate the potential effect of such errors on the electric field distribution. In this work we focus on determining the effect of errors in automatic segmentation of hepatic vessels on the electric field distribution in electroporation-based treatments in the liver. First, a numerical analysis was performed on a simple 'sphere and cylinder' model for tumors and vessels of different sizes and relative positions. Second, an analysis of two models extracted from medical images of real patients in which we introduced variations of an error of the automatic vessel segmentation method was performed. The results obtained from a simple model indicate that ignoring the vessels when calculating the electric field distribution can cause insufficient coverage of the tumor with electric fields. Results of this study indicate that this effect happens for small (10 mm) and medium-sized (30 mm) tumors, especially in the absence of a central electrode inserted in the tumor. The results obtained from the real-case models also show higher negative impact of automatic vessel segmentation errors on the electric field distribution when the central electrode is absent. However, the average error of the automatic vessel segmentation did not have an impact on the electric field distribution if the central electrode was present. This suggests the algorithm is robust enough to be used in creating a model for treatment parameter optimization, but with a central electrode.

records.title: Trajectory optimization for the planning of percutaneous radiofrequency ablation of hepatic tumors
records.abstract: Radiofrequency ablation is increasingly used in the treatment of hepatic tumors. Planning the percutaneous intervention is essential and particularly difficult. In this paper, we focus on an automated computation of optimal needle insertion in computer-assisted surgery with 3D visualization. First, we review our method which delineates on the skin of a virtual patient the candidate zones for needle insertion, i.e., those which allow safe access to the tumor. In each case, we look for the trajectory that minimizes the volume of burnt tissue. Secondly, we introduce a quasi-exhaustive method that allies sampling and certified minimization to form a strong argument for the accuracy of our results. We also compare results of applying both methods on 7 representative reconstructed patient cases.

records.title: A combination segmentation for liver tumors based on CT images
records.abstract: Objective To improve segmental resection accuracy of the liver tumor with CT images. Methods The combination of binaryzation processing,region growth method and boundary segmentectomy were adopted,image noise reduction and edge sharpering were performed. A total of 26 liver tumor CT images were segmented and verfied the feasibility of the method. Results The liver tumors were accurately segmented in CT images,the better segmentectomy effects were achieved for the liver tumor in CT images with clear outline and the surrounding tissue. Most cases achieved the desired segmentectomy,but a large obvious difference between CT images and actual situation of tumor was found in a few cases. Conclusion The combination segmentectomy has a certain effect in liver tumor,but it has limitations in some tumors,especially in the tumors with massive adhesion of surrounding tissue.

records.title: Advances in Deep Learning and Image Processing for Brain Tumor Detection and Classification: A Comprehensive Review
records.journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
records.abstract: Brain tumor identification and classification by the application of deep learning and sophisticated image-processing techniques have been receiving a lot of attention in the medical field. Accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient outcome rely on the accurate identification and differentiation of brain tumors, such as gliomas, meningiomas, and metastases. The most recent developments in deep learning-based techniques for brain tumor identification and categorization by applying medical imaging data, including Computed Tomography (CT). This study looks at CT and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). The main topic of this study is the general theory and developments in deep learning methods for the identification and classification of brain tumors. It investigates how the precision and efficacy of tumor detection can be increased through a variety of models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The paper emphasizes the Significance of applying novel deep-learning techniques for facilitating precise and automated brain tumor identification for individualized treatment, with an emphasis on important achievements, challenges, and opportunities in the area.

records.title: Robots for CT-guided needle insertion: clinical implementation and future perspectives
records.abstract: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

records.title: Comprehensive motion management for liver SBRT on a 1.5 T MR-Linac: Initial clinical experience and dosimetric comparison with an ITV-based workflow
records.abstract: Background and purpose Respiratory-gated MR-guided workflows enable expiration-gated liver stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) based on real-time intrafraction target monitoring. We evaluated the dosimetric impact and early clinical feasibility of this approach by comparing clinically delivered expiration-gated plans with retrospectively generated non-gated ITV-based plans. Methods The first 20 consecutive patients treated with online adaptive MR-guided SBRT for primary or secondary liver malignancies on a 1.5 T MR-Linac between October 2024 and April 2025 were included. Five patients had two lesions, treated with separate plans in two patients, resulting in 22 matched plan pairs. For each clinically delivered gated plan, a retrospective ITV-based plan with identical prescription dose was generated. Paired differences were tested with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and p -values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. The dose–volume analysis was considered exploratory. Results Median planning target volume was lower with the gated workflow than with ITV-based planning (28.0 vs. 41.9 cc). Organ-at-risk constraint violations were fewer with the gated workflow (10 vs. 19), with 11 violations resolved and 2 newly occurring. PTV D98% did not differ significantly ( p = 0.41), although one gated and four ITV-based plans showed PTV D98% < 95%. Uninvolved liver dose was significantly lower with the gated workflow (median Dmean difference 0.97 Gy and 0.93 Gy for three- and five-fraction plans; adjusted p ≤ 0.037). Among 93 evaluable fractions, the mean plan-level median active delivery time was 7.6 min for three-fraction and 6.7 min for five-fraction treatments. Conclusion Expiration-gated MR-guided liver SBRT reduced target volumes and improved normal tissue sparing without compromising target coverage or routine clinical feasibility.

records.title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): An Itch Receptor Drives Melanoma
records.abstract: Mas-Related GPCR X4 (MRGPRX4) is a sensory neuron-restricted receptor for cholestatic itch. Here, we identify MRGPRX4 as an unexpected melanoma driver. MRGPRX4 is upregulated in melanoma and is confined to invasive, neural-crest-like and pre-EMT states associated with dedifferentiation and therapy resistance. Ectopic MRGPRX4 expression in mouse melanocytes drives 100% penetrant, highly metastatic melanoma, demonstrating oncogenic behavior. MRGPRX4 promotes melanoma cell proliferation and invasion through basal, ligand-independent, PI3K-AKT-MAPK activation. Multi-omics links MRGPRX4 expression to a mesenchymal/neural-crest–like program that defines a distinct invasive MRGPRX4+ niche. Comparing transcptomics of MRGPRX4-driven tumors shows a broad overlap with BRAF/NRAS-driven tumors; however, the MRGPRX4 model also enriches an ECM-rich, invasive neural crest–like melanoma state. MRGPRX4 further remodels the tumor microenvironment toward an immunosuppressive, checkpoint-high state enriched in suppressive myeloid cells. Pharmacologic MRGPRX4 inhibition suppresses basal signaling and limits melanoma growth and invasion. In sum, melanoma exploits MRGPRX4 to acquire an invasive and immunosuppressive phenotype, nominating this somatosensory GPCR as a promising therapeutic target.
